messages:
sarah: Heads up — SnapDesk (tenant snapsvc) opened a support escalation: intermittent 504s and p95 spikes on the hosted API since 09:12 PST. Customer pasted failing curl: `curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>'` -> HTTP/1.1 504. They see p95 ~7-9s before 504s.

jordan: On it. Can you share sample request-id(s) and traffic pattern?

sarah: sample req ids: req-9a3f, req-9a4b, req-9a8c. Customer says they rolled a marketing campaign ~09:10 with long prompts (avg token ~1.2k) and concurrency ~30.

raj: Quick telemetry: I pulled shard metrics for snapsvc. queue_depth spiked to 1024 (our configured max), continuous-batcher backlog increased steadily, p95 generation latency hit 7.8s, and upstream gateway timeouts at 30s didn't trigger but our gateway returns 504 after 8s on the hosted path. Metrics: `queue_wait_p95=4.2s`, `gen_p95=7.8s`, `batch_window_current=100ms` for that shard. Kv-cache miss rate high -> lots of spinups.

mei: Customer confirms long sequences + high concurrency. They said requests are synchronous and can't reduce length quickly.

infra-bot: ALERT: hosted-gateway-504-rate > 5% for tenant snapsvc on shard s-7.

jordan: Immediate mitigations I suggest: (1) apply temporary tenant throttling to 8-10 rps, (2) route snapsvc to a larger pool (gpu-xl) for burst, (3) reduce batch window to 20ms for that shard so backlog reduces, (4) enable immediate-schedule fallback if queue wait >250ms. Can ops apply (1) and (3) now?

sarah: I'll apply throttling now and message the customer. Applying ratecap=10rps on snapsvc...

sarah: Throttle applied. Notifying customer: "We've applied a temporary rate cap while we investigate — you should see errors drop within a few minutes."

raj: After throttle: queue_depth dropped to ~180, p95 fell to 1.9s within 2 minutes, 504s dropped to near 0. Good short-term relief.

raj: Root cause summary: sustained high concurrency of long-sequence requests caused continuous-batcher to batch many long traces; KV-cache cold starts added ~200-400ms per request and compounded queue build-up. Our max_queue_depth=1024 was reached for that shard so incoming requests were getting early-failed by gateway timeouts. Autoscaler lag + batch_window tuning (100ms) amplified the tail latency.

mei: Customer asks for timeline to avoid this happening again. They want a permanent fix or patterns to avoid SLO hits.

raj: Proposed longer-term fixes: 
- increase shard queue depth to 2048 temporarily for impacted shards (tradeoff: memory).
- tenant-aware batching: detect longseq tenant and use smaller batch window or immediate scheduling.
- proactive KV-cache prewarm for tenants flagged by long token profiles (prewarm on burst detection).
- autoscaler fast-path: faster scale-up for sustained queue growth >75% for 2 minutes.
- add guardrail: if queue_wait >250ms, bypass continuous-batcher and schedule immediate to avoid head-of-line blocking.

jordan: I'll open an incident ticket and add these as action items. Also adding a docs snippet for CS teams: run the repro and recommended mitigations.

infra-bot: Runbook created: R-12345 (queue-saturation-tail-latency).

sarah: Repro notes (jordan/raj please confirm): run a load-generator against hosted endpoint with 30 concurrent clients, avg tokens ~1200, sustained >12 rps for 3+ minutes -> continuous-batcher backlog forms, queue_depth climbs to max and p95 jumps to >5s, gateway 504s follow.

jordan: Confirmed. I'll add a small script to the runbook and attach load profile.

mei: Customer accepts temporary throttle and asks for SLO credit. I'll escalate to CS.

sarah: I've told them we'll provide an update within 24h and that engineering is tracking fixes.

raj: Short-term mitigation checklist that I'd like op to keep in runbook: 1) apply tenant throttle 2) reduce batch window for shard 3) trigger fast-scale (if pool supports) 4) optionally move tenant to dedicated pool if recurring.

jordan: Adding follow-ups: Ticket ENG-8472 for tenant-aware batching; ENG-8473 for kv-cache prewarm; OPS-432 for autoscale fast-path.

mei: Noting customer prefers dedicated capacity if we can show cost estimate.

sarah: Closing Slack loop — customer updated. Will post incident update and summary in #incidents. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
